claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi HEA coatings initially have a uniform FCC structure with potential metastability.
Mechanical pre-straining can induce localized FCC-to-HCP transformation zones in CoCrFeMnNi coatings.
Applied stress activates a TRIP mechanism in metastable CoCrFeMnNi coatings.
The activated TRIP mechanism involves an FCC-to-HCP phase transformation.
HCP martensitic zones absorb mechanical energy during wear.
HCP martensitic zones act as internal barriers to crack propagation.
The transformed zones deflect or blunt propagating cracks.
Energy absorption and crack deflection or blunting by HCP zones reduce wear.
Pre-strained coatings containing induced HCP will have lower wear rates than as-deposited FCC coatings.
Pre-strained coatings containing induced HCP will show less crack propagation than as-deposited FCC coatings.
The wear-resistance improvement will be greatest at moderate applied loads that induce transformation without causing excessive damage.
Untreated as-deposited FCC coatings have higher wear rates because they lack energy-absorbing HCP zones.
Below the transformation-initiation stress, pre-straining will not provide the proposed benefit.
At sufficiently high applied stress, excessive damage can eliminate the proposed benefit.
Changes in coating composition or microstructure can alter transformation behavior.
Local composition and microstructural defects may affect transformation kinetics and the transformation's contribution to wear performance.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that pre-straining may fail to induce transformation when load is too low, or may cause excessive damage when load is too high, without invalidating the mechanism within its operative range. The falsification rule nevertheless treats failure of controlled pre-straining to increase HCP fraction as sufficient to falsify the hypothesis, without first establishing that the tested load lies inside that operative range.
